questions.stem: How does the woman describe her previous company's culture?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士如何描述她以前公司的文化?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The problem with a company culture that prizes directness above all else is that it creates a toxic culture of brilliant jerks that drives people out and erodes itself from within. 一种把“直接”奉为高于一切的公司文化，问题在于它会造就一种由“才华横溢的混蛋”构成的 有毒文化，逼走员工，并从内部把自己腐蚀掉。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者亲口的定性词。女士在谈她前公司时，自己直接说出 it creates a toxic culture， “toxic”就是她对那种文化的定性，是被问一方的直接评价，正是答案句的信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: it creates a toxic culture ↔Toxic. 原句形容词直接成选项

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 录音确实念了 in the name of efficiency，efficient 听着耳熟极易勾选；但那是说前公司 “打着效率的旗号”给苛刻反馈，是手段不是女士对文化的评价，属典型原词陷阱。 借用原文：in the name of efficiency C) 张冠李戴 Tolerant（宽容）更接近男士公司“accommodating and kind”那种“迁就”的描述，张冠李 戴到女士的前公司头上了；女士前公司的特点是“直接”，不是宽容。 借用原文：accommodating and kind A) 未提及 Weird（古怪）在录音里没有任何对应，女士对前公司的评价是“toxic”而非“古怪”，属无中 生有。

questions.stem: What does the man say about his company's managers?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士如何评价他公司的管理者?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: My company's managers tend to be accommodating and kind, overlooking mistakes or issues so as not to hurt feelings. 我们公司的管理者往往随和又和善，会忽略错误或问题，免得伤了大家的感情。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 男士直接陈述自家管理者。男士主语直接是 My company's managers tend to be accommodating，紧扣题问的“他公司的管理者”，是说话人对该对象的直接陈述句，定位 明确。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: accommodating and kind ↔They are accommodating. 原文形容词直接入选项

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 偷换概念 ignorant（无知）与录音里多次出现的 "overlooking/ignored”（忽略）读音、含义都沾 边，听到 overlooking mistakes 极易误推成“无知”；但男士说的是管理者“故意忽略问题”， 不是“无知”，是音/义双重误导。 借用原文：overlooking mistakes or issues A) 与原文相反 Arrogant（傲慢）与男士说的“accommodating and kind”（随和和善）完全相反，男士对 自家管理者并无负面评价，选它等于把意思听反了。 借用原文：accommodating and kind C) 未提及 Ambitious（有野心/有抱负）在男士谈管理者的话里没有任何对应，男士说的是“随和、怕 伤感情”，与“野心”无关，属无中生有。

options.label: B

questions.stem: What does the woman say the employees in her new company can do?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士说她新公司的员工能做什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Employees have the power to speak up, give feedback, disagree and discuss problems in real time. 员工有权当场发声、给出反馈、表达不同意见并讨论问题。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 授权表达 have the power to。Employees have the power to speak up 用“have the power to”明确点出员工“有权做某事”，正是“can do”题要找的授权信号，后面罗列的动作即 答案来源。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: speak up, give feedback, disagree ↔They can air their views. 概括同义改写

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: D) 未提及 flexible hours（弹性工时）听着像职场福利、很诱人，但录音通篇讲的是“反馈/发声”，从 没提工作时间，属凭印象脑补的无中生有。 C) 过度推断 break conventions（打破常规）比原文的“disagree/speak up”拔得过高，员工只是“能表 异议、讨论问题”，并没有说他们“打破常规”，是过度推断。 借用原文：disagree and discuss problems A) 未提及 think big（有大格局/想大事）原文没有对应，员工被赋予的是“发声、给反馈”的权利，与 “想得大”无关，属无中生有兼拔高。

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D

questions.stem: What does the man say about constructive feedback?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士如何评价建设性反馈?
questions.answerText: It enables people to learn and grow.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow. 毕竟，建设性反馈正是我们学习和成长的途径。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 结论口吻 after all + is how we。Constructive feedback, after all, is how we learn and grow 用 after all 引出总结、is how we 给出定性结论，是男士对反馈作用下的核心论断， 正是“It can…”题要找的结论句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: is how we learn and grow ↔It enables people to learn and grow. 句式转换同义

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 录音里 mindset 确实被念到——但那是女士说的 people need to shift their mindsets （人要转变接受反馈的心态），不是男士说“反馈能改变心态”；既不是男士说的，作用对象 也不同，属张冠李戴式原词陷阱。 借用原文：people need to shift their mindsets D) 未提及 critical thinking（批判性思维）原文从未出现，男士说的是“学习与成长”，硬扯到“批判性 思维”是无中生有兼概念拔高。 B) 未提及 new discoveries（新发现）录音里没有任何对应，男士谈的是反馈对“育儿、友谊、职业发 展”的益处，与“新发现”无关，属未提及。 1 W: How was your holiday? Not too many other tourists around, were there? W: 你的假期怎么样？周围游客不太多吧？ 2 M: No, very few relatively. But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place. It made me realize that indecision is a big problem for me. Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot. M: 是的，相对来说很少。但我发现自己不停地换住处，想找到完美的地方。这让我意识到优柔寡断对我 来说是个大问题。我没有放松，而是一直在寻找最佳地点。 3 W: It seems you suffer from "Fear of Better Options." I've read about it. It describes this loop of indecision as part of our programming. Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process, because as human beings, we are hard-wired to optimize. We have always looked to get the best things we can as a sort of survival of the fittest. Optimizing isn't the problem, but rather the process that we go through. W: 看来你患上了"更好选择恐惧症"。我读到过相关内容。它把这种优柔寡断的循环描述为我们天性的一 部分。本质上，我们有这种倾向，会不断延长决策过程，因为作为人类，我们天生就要追求最优化。我 们一直试图获得最好的东西，这是一种适者生存。追求最优化本身不是问题，问题在于我们经历的这个 过程。 4 M: Well, that makes me feel better. But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization. We can now see what we could have, how we might get it, and what others have that we might want. We keep looking over and return to the same options again and again. M: 嗯，这让我感觉好点了。但我认为多亏了科技，我们可以更容易地进行比较，能接触到更多选择和定 制化服务。我们现在可以看到自己能拥有什么，如何得到它，以及别人拥有什么我们可能想要的东西。我 们不断地查看，一次又一次地回到同样的选项上。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 5 W: Yes. "Fear of Better Options" offers little benefit. It's an ailment of abundance. You must have choices to have that fear of missing out on better options. W: 是的。"更好选择恐惧症"几乎没什么好处。这是富足的副作用。你必须有选择，才会害怕错过更好的 选项。 6 M: Yes, I need to note when I'm worrying about inconsequential things, I guess. If I'm spending too much time worrying over what to have for lunch, I'm robbing myself of the energy to focus on the things that matter. M: 是的，我想我需要注意自己什么时候在为无关紧要的事情担忧。如果我花太多时间纠结午饭吃什么， 我就是在剥夺自己专注于重要事情的精力。 7 W: Exactly. But for more important matters, I think gut instinct might be overrated. When you have 30 odd options, trusting your gut is not practical. What you need to do is research: have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can. The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again. W: 没错。但对于更重要的事情，我认为直觉可能被高估了。当你有三十多个选项时，相信直觉是不现实 的。你需要做的是研究：建立一个流程，投入时间探索你的选项，尽可能多地排除一些东西。决策中最有 害的部分就是一遍又一遍地重复考虑同样的选项。

options.textZh: 它能改变人们的思维方式。

options.label: B
options.text: It can lead to new discoveries.
options.textZh: 它能带来新发现。

options.label: C
options.text: It enables people to learn and grow.

options.text: It is conducive to critical thinking.

questions.stem: What does the man say about his holiday?
questions.stemZh: 男士对他的假期有何评价？
questions.answerText: He kept looking for the best place to stay.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another, trying to find the perfect place. Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot. 但我发现自己从一个住处搬到另一个住处，想找到那个完美的地方。我没有放松，而是一直 在找最好的落脚点。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 转折 But + 对比 Instead of。答案句的信号是双重的：先有转折 But I found myself moving from one accommodation to another，把"假期"的真实状态从"轻松"拽向"折 腾"；再有对比 Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot，明说"不是放松、而 是在找最好的"——转折与"Instead of A, B"句式叠加处，正是他对假期的真正定调。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: trying to find the perfect place ↔looking for the best place to stay perfect=best，place 同指住处 moving from one accommodation to another ↔He kept looking 反复搬=持续地找(kept)

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: C) 与原文相反 C 的 He had a great time sightseeing and relaxing. 偷了录音里的原词 relaxing 来勾你 选，可原文是 Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot——relaxing 前面正 挂着 Instead of（不是…而是），意思恰恰是"没在放松"。听到 relaxing 就选，正好掉 进"原词被否定"的坑。 借用原文：Instead of relaxing, I was looking for the best spot B) 原词陷阱 B 的 He met many tourists from other countries. 听上去呼应开头那句 Not too many other tourists around, were there? 里的 tourists，但原文男士回答的是 No, very few relatively（游客很少），并未说"遇到很多别国游客"；这是借 tourists 一词做的答非所问。 借用原文：No, very few relatively D) 未提及 D 的 He managed to visit a different city each day. 描绘"每天去不同城市"，但男士全程 只谈"换住处找最好的"（accommodation / best spot），从没提过"每天换城市"。它 用"不停移动"的画面感来诱你联想，实属未提及。

options.textZh: 他一直在寻找最好的住处。

options.label: B
options.text: He met many tourists from other countries.

questions.stem: What does the woman say people tend to do when making decisions?
questions.stemZh: 女士说人们在做决定时往往会做什么？
questions.answerText: Stretch out the process in search of the optimal.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Essentially, we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process, because as human beings, we are hard-wired to optimize. 本质上，我们有一种不断拖长决策过程的倾向，因为作为人类，我们天生就被设定为追求 最优。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: tendency to + 总结词 Essentially。答案信号是"总结+点天性"：Essentially（本质上） 领出结论，紧跟 we have this tendency to keep stretching out the decision-making process 直接点出"人有拖长决策过程的倾向"，tendency 正对题干 tend to；后半 because…hard-wired to optimize 补出"为什么"，整句就是"人们做决定时倾向做什么"的 标准答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: keep stretching out the decision-making process ↔Stretch out the process 近乎同形，只略作删减 hard-wired to optimize ↔in search of the optimal optimize 与 optimal 同根，动词转名词

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 A 的 Prioritize what is essential to their best advantage. 用 best advantage 蹭整段反 复出现的 best/optimize 之感，但原文说的是"人会拖长过程"，不是"优先抓要紧事"； prioritize（优先排序）这层意思原文从未提及，是借相近语感造的干扰。 C) 偷换概念 C 的 Deliberate the consequences that may occur.（仔细考虑可能的后果）听着也像"决 策时的做法"，但原文 hard-wired to optimize 讲的是"追求最优"，根本没提"权衡后果"， consequences 是凭空添的概念。 借用原文：hard-wired to optimize D) 未提及 D 的 Take all relevant factors into consideration. 是个放哪都对的万能说法，但原文女士 说的是"人倾向拖长过程"，并未说"人会把所有相关因素都纳入考虑"；它靠"听起来很对"诱 选，实为未提及。

options.label: A
options.text: Prioritize what is essential to their best advantage.
options.textZh: 优先考虑对自己最有利的关键事项。

options.label: B
options.text: Stretch out the process in search of the optimal.
options.textZh: 延长过程以寻求最优选择。

options.label: C
options.text: Deliberate the consequences that may occur.
options.textZh: 考虑可能发生的后果。

options.label: D
options.text: Take all relevant factors into consideration.
options.textZh: 将所有相关因素纳入考虑。

questions.stem: What has made decision making increasingly difficult?
questions.stemZh: 是什么使决策变得越来越困难？

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But I think thanks to technology, we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization. We keep looking over and return to the same options again and again. 但我觉得，多亏了科技，我们能更容易地做比较，能接触到更多选择和定制。我们一遍又一 遍地翻看、回到同样的选项上。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果信号 thanks to。答案信号是因果短语 thanks to technology——thanks to（多亏、 由于）直接引出原因 technology，其后 we can make comparisons more easily and have more access to choice and customization 说明科技带来"选择更多、更难定"的后 果，正是"什么让决策变难"的答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: thanks to technology ↔Modern technology technology 加修饰 Modern，同指一物 have more access to choice and customization ↔Modern technology "选择变多"是科技致难的内在理由

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 A 的 Time pressure. 是"做事难"时最顺常识的猜想，但录音从头到尾没把"时间压力"列为决 策变难的原因，反倒第 7 段女士主张"要投入时间去研究"；Time pressure 纯属凭常识脑 补，未提及。 B) 未提及 B 的 Tight budget. 把成因引向"钱不够"，但全程谈的是"选择太多、反复纠结"，从没提过 预算或花钱，属凭空添加的原因，未提及。 D) 未提及 D 的 Fierce competition. 同属"现代社会通病"类词、听感和 Modern technology 一样"像 那么回事"，但录音从未把 competition 当成决策变难的原因，是借相近气质设的干扰，未 提及。

options.textZh: 时间压力。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 预算紧张。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 现代技术。

questions.stem: According to the woman, what should people do when making important decisions?
questions.stemZh: 根据女士的说法，人们在做重要决定时应该怎么做？
questions.answerText: Avoid going over the same options repeatedly.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: What you need to do is research: have a process, invest time exploring your options, and eliminate as many things as you can. The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again. 你需要做的是去研究：有一套流程，投入时间去探索你的各种选项，并尽可能多地排除掉一 些。决策中最有害的部分，就是一遍又一遍地翻来覆去看同样的选项。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 建议句 What you need to do + 最高级 most toxic。答案信号有两处：What you need to do is research 是直接的建议句（你需要做的是…），亮出女士的主张；而真正对上 B 的 是最高级评价 The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again——most toxic（最有害）点明"反复纠结同一批选项"是最该避免 的，反推出"应避免反复纠结"这一建议。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: The most toxic part of decision making is going over the same options time and time again ↔ Avoid going over the same options repeatedly "最有害"=应避免，肯否定转换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A 的 Research as many different options as possible. 偷用了原文 What you need to do is research 的 research 来诱选，但女士的 research 强调的是"有流程、投入时间、并 eliminate 排除掉尽量多的选项"，而非 as many…as possible（尽可能多地研究选项）；A 把"排除"说反成"尽量多留"，且没体现题问的"重要决定"落点，属盗原词的答非所问。 借用原文：eliminate as many things as you can C) 原词陷阱 C 的 Focus on what is practical. 用了原文出现的 practical，但原文是 When you have 30 odd options, trusting your gut is not practical——practical 是用来说"凭直觉不实 际"的，并非建议"专注于实际的事"；选项截走 practical 一词另造主张，属原词被挪用。 借用原文：trusting your gut is not practical D) 与原文相反 D 的 Trust their gut instinct. 直接搬来原文的 gut，但女士明说 gut instinct might be overrated、trusting your gut is not practical——直觉被高估、不实际，是被否定的做 法。听到 gut instinct 就选，正中"先抬后否"的陷阱。 借用原文：gut instinct might be overrated Section B 1 The role of homework in classrooms is not a new debate. Many parents and teachers are ardent supporters of homework. But do all students benefit from homework? A 2006 research paper suggested some correlation between the amount of homework done by a student and future academic achievement for middle and high school students but not so much for younger kids. 课堂作业的作用并非新的争论话题。许多家长和教师都是作业的坚定支持者。但是所有学生都能从作业中 受益吗？2006年的一项研究论文表明,学生完成的作业量与未来学业成就之间存在一定相关性,这对初中和 高中生适用,但对年幼的孩子则不那么明显。 Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. 2 A Stanford study in 2014 suggested the same was true for students in California's affluent communities. The findings challenged the idea that homework was "inherently good." The researchers concluded that there was an upper limit to the correlation between homework and achievement, suggesting that high school students shouldn't be doing more than two hours of homework a night. And the most valuable kind of homework for elementary-level children was simply assigned free reading. 2014年Stanford的一项研究表明,对于加州富裕社区的学生也是如此。该研究结果挑战了作业"本质上是好 的"这一观点。研究人员得出结论,作业与成就之间的相关性存在上限,表明高中生每晚做作业的时间不应超 过两小时。而对小学阶段儿童来说,最有价值的作业形式就是布置自由阅读。 3 The topic gets more complicated when we talk about the divide between rural and urban communities. Studies found that in remote areas, the poor quality or lack of internet access can put students at a disadvantage because 70% of teachers in these areas assign homework that requires internet access. But one in three households doesn't have internet. His maiden rocket voyage lasted a mere 3 seconds. It scaled an altitude of only 12 meters. Nonetheless, it was a milestone in rocket science. 1926年3月,Goddard在他家乡马萨诸塞州一位姑妈的农场发射了他的第一枚火箭。他的首次火箭飞行仅 持续了3秒。它只达到了12米的高度。尽管如此,这是火箭科学的一个里程碑。 4 Goddard later consulted with a weather expert and determined that the climate of New Mexico was ideal for year-round rocket launches. Over time, Goddard's rocket grew more sophisticated and included the installation of instruments. 然而,这位雄心勃勃的科学家从政府那里获得的支持微乎其微。富有的商人Daniel Guggenheim为 Goddard提供了四年的资助,每年25000美元,以追求他的梦想。其他火箭爱好者也为他筹集了资金。随着 时间的推移,Goddard的火箭变得更加复杂,包括安装了仪器。 6 In spite of his many successes, Goddard was never able to interest the US military in rocket-propelled weapons. The person to thank for that passion and excitement is almost always the entrepreneur. 为新创企业工作伴随着诸多风险。有不稳定性、职责不明确，以及需要成为多面手。但主要好处通常是与 在一家前景光明的新公司中发挥作用相关的热情和兴奋感。几乎总是应该感谢创业者带来了这种热情和兴 奋感。 2 There's something about the founder's energy and enthusiasm that infects the rest of the team. The willingness to take risks may inspire others to be more courageous. The optimism and positivity may motivate people to focus less on trivial and unimportant matters. This was recently tested in research, which analyzed the teams of 73 new companies across a range of industries such as IT, medicine and energy. The CEOs were consulted once again, years after the initial analysis. And most shared their firm's performance reports, so that their success could be more objectively measured. 但尚未得到证明的是创始人的热情是否会导致团队绩效的提升。这在最近的一项研究中得到了检验,该研究 分析了IT、医药和能源等一系列行业中73家新公司的团队。在初步分析数年后,CEO们再次接受了咨询。 大多数人分享了他们公司的业绩报告,以便能够更客观地衡量他们的成功。 5 Entrepreneurial teams generally progress through three phases. The first is inventing a product or service, the second is founding the venture to sell that product or service, and the third is developing the firm so it continues to grow. 创业团队通常经历三个阶段。第一个是发明产品或服务,第二个是创立企业来销售该产品或服务,第三个是 发展公司使其持续增长。 6 The researchers discovered that when the team is passionate about the third phase—developing the firm—there's a clear link to performance. But the first phase—a passion for invention—is not a reliable indicator that the firm will still be open for business a few years later. Likewise, the second—a passion for founding the venture—doesn't necessarily translate into great success. 研究人员发现,当团队对第三阶段——发展公司——充满热情时,与绩效之间存在明确的联系。但第一阶段 ——对发明的热情——并不是公司几年后仍在营业的可靠指标。同样,第二阶段——对创立企业的热情 ——也不一定转化为巨大成功。 7 The solution to great team performance stems from a willingness to recruit others who could direct their passion towards the third phase of entrepreneurialism: developing the business. Employing more staff can in itself be a risk for an entrepreneur, as is paying them big dollars to attract them. On many occasions, the entrepreneurs reported not paying themselves a wage at all initially, in order to cover salaries and expenses. 实现卓越团队绩效的解决方案源于愿意招募能够将热情导向创业第三阶段的其他人:发展业务。雇用更多员 工本身对创业者来说就是一种风险,支付高薪来吸引他们也是如此。在许多情况下,创业者报告说最初根本 不给自己支付工资,以支付员工薪水和费用。

analysis.text: What does the author imply about the various gadgets on cars 中 imply 是典型推断 信号，要求在原文未明说的方向上做一步延伸。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What does the author imply about X 标准句式，结构无难度，关键是认出 imply 的题型 信号。

analysis.label: 选项

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What key message does the author try to convey in the passage——疑问句倒装，主 语 the author，谓语 try to convey，宾语 what key message，结构清楚不绕。 55. B) There is always a price to pay to develop technology for a better world. C) Technological innovation should be properly regulated. D) The culture of Silicon Valley ought not to be emulated.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 全文核心是要正视技术后果、加以监管，而非"不必夸大后果"——选项的方向与作者完 全相反。 B) 以偏概全 原文确实承认有代价（unforeseen and unintended consequences），但作者的核心 立场不是"代价不可避免"，而是"需要监管"。把局部当作主旨，落点偏移。 C) ✓ 正确 thoughtful regulation is necessary for a better future ↔ Technological innovation should be properly regulated Central control and collective organisation can produce smoother and fairer outcomes ↔ Technological innovation should be properly regulated 预判要的"技术需妥善监管"，C 把 thoughtful regulation 直译为 properly regulated，又覆盖了 central control 这条中段证据，是全文主线的最大公约数。 D) 以偏概全 硅谷文化只在 Silicon Valley has to acknowledge the costs of the intoxicating hurry 一句被点到，作为例子；全文主旨并非反对硅谷文化本身。

A) Notre Dame Cathedral in the heart of Paris was within "15 to 30 minutes" of complete destruction as firefighters battled to stop flames reaching its bell towers on Monday evening, French authorities have revealed. A greater disaster was averted by members of the Paris fire brigade, who risked their lives to remain inside the burning monument to create a wall of water between the raging fire and the two towers on the west of the building.
B) The revelation of how close France came to losing its most famous cathedral emerged as police investigators questioned workers involved in the restoration of the monument to try to establish the cause of the devastating blaze. Paris prosecutor Remy Heitz said that an initial fire alert was sounded at 6:20 pm on Monday evening but no fire was found. The second alert was sounded at 6:43 pm, and the blaze was discovered on the roof.
C) More than €650 million was raised in a few hours on Tuesday as French business leaders and global corporations announced they would donate to a restoration campaign launched by the president, Emmanuel Macron. But as the emergency services picked through the burnt debris, a row was resurfacing over accusations that the beloved cathedral, immortalised in Victor Hugo's novel, was already crumbling before the fire.
D) The cathedral is owned by the French state and has been at the centre of a years-long dispute over who should finance restoration work of the collapsing staircases, crumbling statues and cracked walls. Jean-Michel Leniaud, the president of the scientific council at the National Heritage Institute, said: "What happened was bound to happen. The lack of adequate maintenance and daily attention to such a majestic building is the cause of this catastrophe." After the blaze was declared completely extinguished, 15 hours after it started, the junior interior minister, Laurent Nunez, said the structure had been saved but remained vulnerable. He praised the actions of the firefighters but admitted the fate of the cathedral had been uncertain. "They saved the main structure, but it all came down to 15- 30 minutes," Nunez said.
E) In a surprise televised address on Tuesday evening, Macron said he wanted to see the cathedral rebuilt within five years. "The fire at Notre Dame reminds us that we will always have challenges to overcome," Macron said, "Notre Dame is our history, our literature, the centre of our life. It is the standard by which we measure our distances. It's so many books, so many paintings. It's the cathedral of every French person, even those who have never visited it. This history is ours and so we will rebuild Notre Dame. It is what the French people expect; it is what our history deserves. It is our deep destiny. We will rebuild Notre Dame so it is even more beautiful than before. I want it done in the next five years. We can do it. After the time of testing comes a time of reflection and then of action."
F) The fire, which had started at the base of the 93-metre spire(尖塔) at about 6:40 pm on Monday, spread through the cathedral's roof, made up of hundreds of oak beams, some dating back to the 13th century. These beams, known as la forêt (the forest) because of their density, formed the cross-shaped roof that ran the length of the central part of the cathedral. As hundreds of tourists and Parisians stood and watched the flames leaping from the roof, there was shock and tears as the cathedral spire caught fire, burned and then collapsed into itself.
G) A collection of dramatic videos and photos quickly spread across social media, showing the horrifying destruction, and attracting emotional responses from people all over the world. Indeed, within minutes the fire occupied headlines of every major global newspaper and television network. This is not surprising given Notre Dame Cathedral, meaning "Our Lady", is one of the most recognised symbols of the city of Paris attracting millions of tourists every year.
H) While the world looked on, the 500 firefighters at the scene then battled to prevent the flames from reaching the two main towers, where the cathedral bells hang. If the wooden frame of the towers had caught fire, it could have sent the bells—the largest of which, the Emmanuel Bell, weighs 13 tons— crashing down, potentially causing the collapse of both towers. Police and fire services will spend the next 48 hours assessing the "security and safety" of the 850-year-old structure. Nunez said: "We have identified vulnerabilities throughout the structure, all of which still need securing." As a result, residents of five buildings around the northern side of the cathedral were being temporarily evacuated, he added. Architects have identified three main holes in the structure, in the locations of the spire, the main hall and the upper rooms to the north of the central aisle. Most of the wooden roof beams have been burned, and parts of the concrete holding up the roof have collapsed.
I) The interior minister, Christophe Castaner, visited the cathedral on Tuesday afternoon to see the extent of the devastation. Ash covered the marble diamond-patterned floor and floated in large pools of grey water from the fire hoses. Behind a heap of blackened oak beams that lay piled up where they had fallen, daylight from vast holes in the cathedral roof lit a golden cross over a statue by Nicolas Coustou, which appeared to have escaped damage. Preliminary inspections also suggested the three ornate(装饰华丽的) stained glass "rose" windows appeared to have survived the fire, officials said. However, fire officers have said a complete inventory of the damage will not be possible until the cathedral structure has been deemed safe.
J) The culture minister, Franck Riester, said religious relics saved from the cathedral were being securely held at the Hotel de Ville, and works of art that sustained smoke damage were being taken to the Louvre, the world's largest art museum, where they would be dried out, repaired and stored. Sixteen copper statues that decorated the spire had been removed for restoration only a few days before the fire. Relics at the top of the spire are believed lost as the spire was destroyed. As well as damage from the heat, which firefighters said reached more than 800 ℃, experts also need to assess damage from the vast quantities of water firefighters poured into the cathedral. One casualty of this was The Great Organ constructed in the 1730s, which was said to have escaped the flames but been significantly damaged by water.
K) French political commentators noted the devastating fire had succeeded where Macron had failed in uniting the country. But criticism over the original state of the building is likely to intensify over coming days. Leniaud told La Croix newspaper: "This is not about looking for people to blame. The responsibility is collective because this is the most loved monument in the country." Alexandre Gady, an art historian, agreed. "We've been saying for years that the budget for maintaining historic monuments is too low," Gady said. The Paris prosecutor's office has opened an inquiry into "involuntary destruction by fire", indicating they believe the cause of the blaze was accidental rather than criminal. 36. The total amount of damage to Notre Dame Cathedral can be assessed only when its structure is considered safe.

P1 We often think of drawing as something that takes inborn talent, but this kind of thinking stems from our misclassification of drawing as, primarily, an art form rather than a tool for learning.

P2 Researchers, teachers, and artists are starting to see how drawing can positively impact a wide variety of skills and disciplines.

P3 Most of us have spent some time drawing before, but at some point, most of us stop drawing. There are people who don't, obviously, and thank God for that: a world without designers and artists would be a very shabby one indeed.

P4 Some argue that so many adults have abandoned drawing because we've miscategorized it and given it a very narrow definition. In his book, Stick Figures: Drawing as a Human Practice, Professor D. B. Dowd argues that we have misfiled the significance of drawing because we see it as a professional skill instead of a personal capacity. We mistakenly think of "good" drawings as those which work as Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. recreations of the real world, as realistic illusions. Rather, drawing should be recategorized as a symbolic tool.

P5 Human beings have been drawing for 73,000 years. It's part of what it means to be human. We don't have the strength of chimpanzees(大猩猩) because we've given up animal strength to manipulate subtle instruments, like hammers, spears, and—later—pens and pencils. The human hand is an extremely dense network of nerve endings. In many ways, human beings are built to draw.

P6 Some researchers argue that doodling( 涂画) activates the brain's so-called default circuit— essentially, the areas of the brain responsible for maintaining a baseline level of activity in the absence of other stimuli. Because of this, some believe that doodling during a boring lecture can help students pay attention. In one study, participants were asked to listen to a list of names while either doodling or sitting still. Those who doodled remembered 29 percent more of the names than those who did not.

P7 There's also evidence that drawing talent is based on how accurately someone perceives the world. The human visual system tends to misjudge size, shape, color, and angles but artists perceive these qualities more accurately than non-artists. reading-2.raw:
P1 The car has reshaped our cities. It seems to offer autonomy for everyone. There is something almost delightful in the detachment from reality of advertisements showing mass-produced cars marketed as symbols of individuality and of freedom when most of their lives will be spent making short journeys on choked roads.

P2 For all the fuss made about top speeds, cornering ability and acceleration, the most useful gadgets on a modern car are those which work when you're going very slowly: parking sensors, sound systems, and navigation apps which will show a way around upcoming traffic jams. This seems to be one of the few areas where the benefit of sharing personal information comes straight back to the sharer: because these apps know where almost all the users are, and how fast they are moving almost all the time, they can spot traffic congestion(堵塞) very quickly and suggest ways round it. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P3 The problem comes when everyone is using a navigation app which tells them to avoid everyone else using the same gadget. Traffic jams often appear where no one has enough information to avoid them. When a lucky few have access to the knowledge, they will benefit greatly. But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads that seem to offer a way round them.

P4 This new congestion teaches us two things. The first is that the promises of technology will never be realised as fully as we hope; they will be limited by their unforeseen and unintended consequences. Sitting in a more comfortable car in a different traffic jam is pleasant but hardly the liberation that once seemed to be promised. The second is that self-organisation will not get us where we want to go. The efforts of millions of drivers to get ahead do not miraculously produce a situation in which everyone does better than before, but one in which almost everyone does rather worse. Central control and collective organisation can produce smoother and fairer outcomes, though even that much is never guaranteed.

P5 Similar limits can be foreseen for the much greater advances promised by self-driving cars. Last week, one operated by the taxi company Uber struck and killed a woman pushing her bicycle across a wide road in Arizona. This was the first recorded death involving a car which was supposed to be fully autonomous. Experts have said that it suggests a "catastrophic failure" of technology.

P6 Increasingly, even Silicon Valley has to acknowledge the costs of the intoxicating(令人陶醉的) hurry that characterises its culture. What traffic teaches us is that reckless and uncontrolled change is as likely to harm us as it is to benefit us, and that thoughtful regulation is necessary for a better future.

sentences.text: 三河作同位列举、末段降级为分词状语 长江、黄河和澜沧江 是「中国三大河流」的具体列举，作同位语 China's three major rivers, namely the Yangtze, the Yellow River and the Lancang。最后 在中国的水生态中发挥着重要作 用 可降级为现在分词短语 playing an important role in China's water ecology 作伴随状语，挂 在前面主句后，避免再起一个并列谓语显得松散。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 介词搭配 以…闻名 是固定搭配 be famous / known for（不是 famous as）；发挥重要作用 是 play an important role in（介词 in 不能少）。 冠词 三条河流专名前都要带定冠词 the：the Yangtze, the Yellow River, the Lancang River。 单复数 三大河流 用复数 three major rivers；水资源 water resources 习惯用复数。 时态 三块均为青海当下的客观属性，回指基调用一般现在时（is famous / is the source / playing 隐含 现在）。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Qinghai is especially famous for its abundant water resources. It is the source of China's three major rivers, namely the Yangtze, the Yellow River and the Lancang River, playing an important role in China's water ecology. 英语六级 2021年6月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
